sanskrit: tato vāsagṛhaṃ śubhraṃ pannagendrasya saṃmatam jagāma bhāryām ādāya stūyamāno maharṣibhiḥ
english: Then, taking his wife and praised by great sages, he went to the bright dwelling sanctioned by the lord of serpents.

sanskrit: śayanaṃ tatra vai kḷptaṃ spardhyāstaraṇasaṃvṛtam tatra bhāryāsahāyaḥ sa jaratkārur uvāsa ha
english: There a bed was prepared, covered with splendid coverings; and there Jaratkāru dwelt together with his wife.

sanskrit: sa tatra samayaṃ cakre bhāryayā saha sattamaḥ vipriyaṃ me na kartavyaṃ na ca vācyaṃ kadā cana
english: That best of men made a covenant with his wife there: "What is displeasing to me must never be done, nor ever spoken."

sanskrit: tyajeyam apriye hi tvāṃ kṛte vāsaṃ ca te gṛhe etad gṛhāṇa vacanaṃ mayā yat samudīritam
english: "For if you displease me, I shall abandon you and leave this house of yours. Take to heart this word I have now spoken."

sanskrit: tataḥ paramasaṃvignā svasā nāgapates tu sā atiduḥkhānvitā vācaṃ tam uvācaivam astv iti
english: Then the sister of the serpent lord, deeply agitated and filled with great sorrow, said to him: "So be it."

sanskrit: tathaiva sā ca bhartāraṃ duḥkhaśīlam upācarat upāyaiḥ śvetakākīyaiḥ priyakāmā yaśasvinī
english: And that illustrious woman, ever wishing to please him, tended her difficult-tempered husband by every cautious and discreet means.

sanskrit: ṛtukāle tataḥ snātā kadā cid vāsukeḥ svasā bhartāraṃ taṃ yathānyāyam upatasthe mahāmunim
english: Then once, after her purificatory bath at the proper season, the sister of Vāsuki duly approached her husband, the great sage.

sanskrit: tatra tasyāḥ samabhavad garbho jvalanasaṃnibhaḥ atīva tapasā yukto vaiśvānarasamadyutiḥ śuklapakṣe yathā somo vyavardhata tathaiva saḥ
english: Then within her a child was conceived, blazing like fire, endowed with great ascetic power, brilliant as Vaiśvānara; and it grew like the moon in the bright fortnight.

sanskrit: tataḥ katipayāhasya jaratkārur mahātapāḥ utsaṅge 'syāḥ śiraḥ kṛtvā suṣvāpa parikhinnavat
english: Then after some days Jaratkāru of great austerity, resting his head in her lap, fell into deep sleep as though exhausted.

sanskrit: tasmiṃś ca supte viprendre savitāstam iyād girim ahnaḥ parikṣaye brahmaṃs tataḥ sācintayat tadā vāsuker bhaginī bhītā dharmalopān manasvinī
english: And while that foremost of brahmins slept, the sun moved toward its setting mountain at the close of the day, O brahmin; then Vāsuki's sister, that wise woman, became fearful of a lapse in religious duty and began to reflect.

sanskrit: kiṃ nu me sukṛtaṃ bhūyād bhartur utthāpanaṃ na vā duḥkhaśīlo hi dharmātmā kathaṃ nāsyāparādhnuyām
english: "Would it be right for me to wake my husband, or not? He is righteous yet difficult-tempered — how can I not offend him?"

sanskrit: kopo vā dharmaśīlasya dharmalopo 'tha vā punaḥ dharmalopo garīyān vai syād atrety akaron manaḥ
english: "Either the wrath of this righteous man, or else a lapse in his religious duty — a lapse in religious duty is certainly the graver of the two": thus she resolved in her mind.

sanskrit: utthāpayiṣye yady enaṃ dhruvaṃ kopaṃ kariṣyati dharmalopo bhaved asya saṃdhyātikramaṇe dhruvam
english: "If I wake him, he will certainly be angry; but if the twilight prayer is missed, there will certainly be a breach of his religious duty."

sanskrit: iti niścitya manasā jaratkārur bhujaṃgamā tam ṛṣiṃ dīptatapasaṃ śayānam analopamam uvācedaṃ vacaḥ ślakṣṇaṃ tato madhurabhāṣiṇī
english: Having thus resolved in her mind, that serpent-woman Jaratkāru, the sweet-spoken one, gently addressed the reclining sage of blazing austerity in these words.

sanskrit: uttiṣṭha tvaṃ mahābhāga sūryo 'stam upagacchati saṃdhyām upāssva bhagavann apaḥ spṛṣṭvā yatavrataḥ
english: "Arise, O greatly blessed one — the sun is setting. O lord, touch water and observe the twilight worship, you who are strict in your vows."

sanskrit: prāduṣkṛtāgnihotro 'yaṃ muhūrto ramyadāruṇaḥ saṃdhyā pravartate ceyaṃ paścimāyāṃ diśi prabho
english: "This is the hour when the fire-sacrifice is kindled, both lovely and awesome; and now the twilight prayer begins in the western quarter, O master."

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ sa bhagavāñ jaratkārur mahātapāḥ bhāryāṃ prasphuramāṇoṣṭha idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Thus addressed, the venerable Jaratkāru of great austerity, his lips quivering, spoke these words to his wife.

sanskrit: avamānaḥ prayukto 'yaṃ tvayā mama bhujaṃgame samīpe te na vatsyāmi gamiṣyāmi yathāgatam
english: "This is an insult you have offered me, O serpent-woman. I will not stay with you any longer; I shall go the way I came."

sanskrit: na hi tejo 'sti vāmoru mayi supte vibhāvasoḥ astaṃ gantuṃ yathākālam iti me hṛdi vartate
english: "For it is my firm conviction that while I sleep, the sun Vibhāvasu has no power to set at its proper time, O fair-thighed one."

sanskrit: na cāpy avamatasyeha vastuṃ roceta kasya cit kiṃ punar dharmaśīlasya mama vā madvidhasya vā
english: "Nor would it please anyone who has been insulted to remain here — least of all one of righteous conduct such as I, of my disposition."

sanskrit: evam uktā jaratkārur bhartrā hṛdayakampanam abravīd bhaginī tatra vāsukeḥ saṃniveśane
english: When Jaratkāru was thus addressed by her husband, Vāsuki's sister spoke with a trembling heart in that dwelling.

sanskrit: nāvamānāt kṛtavatī tavāhaṃ pratibodhanam dharmalopo na te vipra syād ity etat kṛtaṃ mayā
english: "It was not out of disrespect that I woke you; I did this so that there might be no breach of your religious duty, O brahmin."

sanskrit: uvāca bhāryām ity ukto jaratkārur mahātapāḥ ṛṣiḥ kopasamāviṣṭas tyaktukāmo bhujaṃgamām
english: Thus addressed by his wife, the great sage Jaratkāru of mighty austerity, seized by anger and resolved to abandon the serpent-woman, spoke.

sanskrit: na me vāg anṛtaṃ prāha gamiṣye 'haṃ bhujaṃgame samayo hy eṣa me pūrvaṃ tvayā saha mithaḥ kṛtaḥ
english: "My word does not speak falsehood — I shall depart, O serpent-woman. For this was the covenant I made with you from the beginning."

sanskrit: sukham asmy uṣito bhadre brūyās tvaṃ bhrātaraṃ śubhe ito mayi gate bhīru gataḥ sa bhagavān iti tvaṃ cāpi mayi niṣkrānte na śokaṃ kartum arhasi
english: "I have dwelt here in happiness, O auspicious one. Tell your brother, O timid one: 'That venerable one has departed from here.' And after I have gone, you too should not grieve."

sanskrit: ity uktā sānavadyāṅgī pratyuvāca patiṃ tadā jaratkāruṃ jaratkāruś cintāśokaparāyaṇā
english: Thus addressed, the blameless-limbed Jaratkāru, overwhelmed with worry and grief, replied to her husband Jaratkāru.

sanskrit: bāṣpagadgadayā vācā mukhena pariśuṣyatā kṛtāñjalir varārohā paryaśrunayanā tataḥ dhairyam ālambya vāmorūr hṛdayena pravepatā
english: With a voice choked with tears, a face pale and dry, eyes brimming with tears, hands folded in supplication, that woman of fair limbs steadied herself with composure though her heart was trembling.

sanskrit: na mām arhasi dharmajña parityaktum anāgasam dharme sthitāṃ sthito dharme sadā priyahite ratām
english: "O knower of dharma, you should not abandon me who am without fault, who stands firm in dharma, who is ever devoted to your welfare and happiness."

sanskrit: pradāne kāraṇaṃ yac ca mama tubhyaṃ dvijottama tad alabdhavatīṃ mandāṃ kiṃ māṃ vakṣyati vāsukhiḥ
english: "And the purpose for which I was given to you, O best of twice-born ones — if I have not achieved that, what will Vāsuki say to wretched me?"

sanskrit: mātṛśāpābhibhūtānāṃ jñātīnāṃ mama sattama apatyam īpṣitaṃ tvattas tac ca tāvan na dṛśyate
english: "The offspring longed for from you for the sake of my kinsmen who are oppressed by their mother's curse, O excellent one — that too has not yet come to be seen."

sanskrit: tvatto hy apatyalābhena jñātīnāṃ me śivaṃ bhavet saṃprayogo bhaven nāyaṃ mama moghas tvayā dvija
english: "Through the gaining of offspring from you, wellbeing would come to my kinsmen; let not this union with you be fruitless for me, O twice-born one."

sanskrit: jñātīnāṃ hitam icchantī bhagavaṃs tvāṃ prasādaye imam avyaktarūpaṃ me garbham ādhāya sattama kathaṃ tyaktvā mahātmā san gantum icchasy anāgasam
english: "Wishing the welfare of my kinsmen, O venerable one, I entreat you — having planted in me this child whose form is not yet manifest, O best of men, how can you, being a great soul, wish to abandon me who am without fault?"

sanskrit: evam uktas tu sa munir bhāryāṃ vacanam abravīt yady uktam anurūpaṃ ca jaratkārus tapodhanaḥ
english: Thus addressed, the sage Jaratkāru, wealth of austerity, spoke an apt and fitting word to his wife.

sanskrit: asty eṣa garbhaḥ subhage tava vaiśvānaropamaḥ ṛṣiḥ paramadharmātmā vedavedāṅgapāragaḥ
english: "This child exists within you, O fortunate one, comparable to Vaiśvānara — a seer of supreme righteousness, versed in the Vedas and all their branches."

sanskrit: evam uktvā sa dharmātmā jaratkārur mahān ṛṣiḥ ugrāya tapase bhūyo jagāma kṛtaniścayaḥ
english: Having spoken thus, that righteous-souled great sage Jaratkāru, firmly resolved, departed again for severe austerities.

sanskrit: sūta uvāca gatamātraṃ tu bhartāraṃ jaratkārur avedayat bhrātus tvaritam āgamya yathātathyaṃ tapodhana
english: The Sūta said: As soon as her husband had departed, Jaratkāru quickly came to her brother and told him the truth of what had happened, O wealth of austerity.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa bhujagaśreṣṭhaḥ śrutvā sumahad apriyam uvāca bhaginīṃ dīnāṃ tadā dīnataraḥ svayam
english: Then that foremost of serpents, having heard the deeply grievous news, spoke to his dejected sister, himself more dejected still.

sanskrit: jānāsi bhadre yat kāryaṃ pradāne kāraṇaṃ ca yat pannagānāṃ hitārthāya putras te syāt tato yadi
english: "You know, dear one, what purpose was to be served and the reason you were given — whether a son would be born to you from him for the welfare of the serpents."

sanskrit: sa sarpasatrāt kila no mokṣayiṣyati vīryavān evaṃ pitāmahaḥ pūrvam uktavān māṃ suraiḥ saha
english: "That valiant one will surely rescue us from the serpent sacrifice — so did the grandfather formerly tell me, together with the gods."

sanskrit: apy asti garbhaḥ subhage tasmāt te munisattamāt na cecchāmy aphalaṃ tasya dārakarma manīṣiṇaḥ
english: "Is there indeed a child in you from that best of sages, O fortunate one? I do not want the act of marriage of that wise one to have been fruitless."

sanskrit: kāmaṃ ca mama na nyāyyaṃ praṣṭuṃ tvāṃ kāryam īdṛśam kiṃ tu kāryagarīyastvāt tatas tvāham acūcudam
english: "Indeed it is not proper for me to question you on such a matter; but because the urgency of the task is paramount, I have thus pressed you."

sanskrit: durvāsatāṃ viditvā ca bhartus te 'titapasvinaḥ nainam anvāgamiṣyāmi kadā cid dhi śapet sa mām
english: "Knowing the difficult nature of your husband, that most austere one, I will not go after him — for he might curse me."

sanskrit: ācakṣva bhadre bhartus tvaṃ sarvam eva viceṣṭitam śalyam uddhara me ghoraṃ bhadre hṛdi cirasthitam
english: "Tell me, dear one, everything your husband did. Remove this terrible thorn that has long been lodged in my heart, O dear one."

sanskrit: jaratkārus tato vākyam ity uktā pratyabhāṣata āśvāsayantī saṃtaptaṃ vāsukiṃ pannageśvaram
english: Then Jaratkāru, thus addressed, replied with words comforting the afflicted Vāsuki, lord of serpents.

sanskrit: pṛṣṭo mayāpatyahetoḥ sa mahātmā mahātapāḥ astīty udaram uddiśya mamedaṃ gatavāṃś ca saḥ
english: "When I asked him for the sake of offspring, that great soul of mighty austerity said 'it exists,' pointing to my womb, and then he departed."

sanskrit: svaireṣv api na tenāhaṃ smarāmi vitathaṃ kva cit uktapūrvaṃ kuto rājan sāṃparāye sa vakṣyati
english: "Even in casual speech I do not recall him ever saying anything false — how then, O king, would he speak falsely in a matter of such consequence?"

sanskrit: na saṃtāpas tvayā kāryaḥ kāryaṃ prati bhujaṃgame utpatsyati hi te putro jvalanārkasamadyutiḥ
english: "You must not grieve regarding the purpose, O serpent lord — your nephew will be born, blazing with the radiance of fire and sun."

sanskrit: ity uktvā hi sa māṃ bhrātar gato bhartā tapovanam tasmād vyetu paraṃ duḥkhaṃ tavedaṃ manasi sthitam
english: "Having said this to me, O brother, my husband went to the forest of austerities; therefore let this great sorrow that lodges in your mind depart."

sanskrit: etac chrutvā sa nāgendro vāsukiḥ parayā mudā evam astv iti tad vākyaṃ bhaginyāḥ pratyagṛhṇata
english: Having heard this, that lord of serpents Vāsuki accepted his sister's words with great joy, saying "So be it."

sanskrit: sāntvamānārthadānaiś ca pūjayā cānurūpayā sodaryāṃ pūjayām āsa svasāraṃ pannagottamaḥ
english: That foremost of serpents honored his sister born of the same womb with comforting words, gifts, and fitting reverence.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa vavṛdhe garbho mahātejā raviprabhaḥ yathā somo dvijaśreṣṭha śuklapakṣodito divi
english: Then that child of mighty radiance, brilliant as the sun, grew in the womb — like the moon risen in the bright fortnight in the sky, O foremost of twice-born ones.

sanskrit: yathākālaṃ tu sā brahman prajajñe bhujagasvasā kumāraṃ devagarbhābhaṃ pitṛmātṛbhayāpaham
english: In due time, O brahmin, that sister of the serpent gave birth to a boy who resembled the embryo of a god, the remover of his father's and mother's fear.

sanskrit: vavṛdhe sa ca tatraiva nāgarājaniveśane vedāṃś cādhijage sāṅgān bhārgavāc cyavanātmajāt
english: And he grew up there in the dwelling of the serpent king; he mastered the Vedas along with their branches from the Bhārgava, the son of Cyavana.

sanskrit: caritavrato bāla eva buddhisattvaguṇānvitaḥ nāma cāsyābhavat khyātaṃ lokeṣv āstīka ity uta
english: Even as a boy he observed his vows, endowed with wisdom, courage, and virtue; and his name became known throughout the worlds as Āstīka.

sanskrit: astīty uktvā gato yasmāt pitā garbhastham eva tam vanaṃ tasmād idaṃ tasya nāmāstīketi viśrutam
english: Because his father departed for the forest saying 'it exists' even while he was still in the womb, therefore his name became celebrated as Āstīka.

sanskrit: sa bāla eva tatrasthaś carann amitabuddhimān gṛhe pannagarājasya prayatnāt paryarakṣyata
english: While still a boy he moved about there, that one of boundless intellect, carefully guarded and protected in the house of the serpent king.

sanskrit: bhagavān iva deveśaḥ śūlapāṇir hiraṇyadaḥ vivardhamānaḥ sarvāṃs tān pannagān abhyaharṣayat
english: Growing up like the venerable lord of the gods, the trident-bearer, the bestower of gold, he filled all those serpents with joy.

sanskrit: śaunaka uvāca yad apṛcchat tadā rājā mantriṇo janamejayaḥ pituḥ svargagatiṃ tan me vistareṇa punar vada
english: Śaunaka said: What king Janamejaya then asked his ministers regarding his father's passing to heaven — tell me that again in full.

sanskrit: sūta uvāca śṛṇu brahman yathā pṛṣṭā mantriṇo nṛpates tadā ākhyātavantas te sarve nidhanaṃ tat parikṣitaḥ
english: The Sūta said: Listen, O brahmin, to how the ministers, being questioned by the king, all narrated the death of Parīkṣit.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca jānanti tu bhavantas tad yathāvṛttaḥ pitā mama āsīd yathā ca nidhanaṃ gataḥ kāle mahāyaśāḥ
english: Janamejaya said: You gentlemen know how my father conducted himself and how that greatly renowned one met his death in due time.

sanskrit: śrutvā bhavatsakāśād dhi pitur vṛttam aśeṣataḥ kalyāṇaṃ pratipatsyāmi viparītaṃ na jātu cit
english: "For having heard from you the full account of my father's life and conduct, I shall pursue what is good and never what is contrary to it."

sanskrit: sūta uvāca mantriṇo 'thābruvan vākyaṃ pṛṣṭās tena mahātmanā sarvadharmavidaḥ prājñā rājānaṃ janamejayam
english: The Sūta said: Then the ministers, questioned by that great-souled one, those learned men versed in all dharma, spoke their words to king Janamejaya.

sanskrit: dharmātmā ca mahātmā ca prajāpālaḥ pitā tava āsīd iha yathāvṛttaḥ sa mahātmā śṛṇuṣva tat
english: "Your father was righteous-souled, great-souled, a protector of his subjects — hear how that great soul conducted himself here."

sanskrit: cāturvarṇyaṃ svadharmasthaṃ sa kṛtvā paryarakṣata dharmato dharmavid rājā dharmo vigrahavān iva
english: "That king, knowing dharma, protected the four social orders established in their own duties, ruling righteously — as though dharma incarnate."

sanskrit: rarakṣa pṛthivīṃ devīṃ śrīmān atulavikramaḥ dveṣṭāras tasya naivāsan sa ca na dveṣṭi kaṃ cana samaḥ sarveṣu bhūteṣu prajāpatir ivābhavat
english: "That glorious one of incomparable valor protected this noble earth; he had no enemies, nor did he hate anyone — equal to all beings, he was like Prajāpati himself."

sanskrit: brāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyā vaiśyāḥ śūdrāś caiva svakarmasu sthitāḥ sumanaso rājaṃs tena rājñā svanuṣṭhitāḥ
english: "Brahmins, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, and śūdras, each established in their proper duties and contented in mind, O king, were well governed by that king."

sanskrit: vidhavānāthakṛpaṇān vikalāṃś ca babhāra saḥ sudarśaḥ sarvabhūtānām āsīt soma ivāparaḥ
english: "He cared for widows, the helpless, the wretched, and the disabled; that fair-looking one was like a second moon to all beings."

sanskrit: tuṣṭapuṣṭajanaḥ śrīmān satyavāg dṛḍhavikramaḥ dhanurvede ca śiṣyo 'bhūn nṛpaḥ śāradvatasya saḥ
english: "His people were content and well-fed; that glorious king was true of speech and firm in valor; he was a student of the science of archery under Śāradvatī's son."

sanskrit: govindasya priyaś cāsīt pitā te janamejaya lokasya caiva sarvasya priya āsīn mahāyaśāḥ
english: "Your father was dear to Govinda, O Janamejaya, and that greatly renowned one was dear to all the world."

sanskrit: parikṣīṇeṣu kuruṣu uttarāyām ajāyata parikṣid abhavat tena saubhadrasyātmajo balī
english: "When the Kurus were all but extinct, he was born of Uttarā; through him, that mighty son of Saubhadra's line, Parīkṣit came to be."

sanskrit: rājadharmārthakuśalo yuktaḥ sarvaguṇair nṛpaḥ jitendriyaś cātmavāṃś ca medhāvī vṛddhasevitaḥ
english: "Skilled in royal dharma and statecraft, endowed with every virtue, that king had conquered his senses, was self-possessed, intelligent, and attended upon by elders."

sanskrit: ṣaḍvargavin mahābuddhir nītidharmavid uttamaḥ prajā imās tava pitā ṣaṣṭiṃ varṣāṇy apālayat tato diṣṭāntam āpannaḥ sarpeṇānativartitam
english: "Master of the six categories, of great intellect, supremely versed in policy and dharma — your father protected these subjects for sixty years, then met his fated end, which could not be turned aside, through a serpent."

sanskrit: tatas tvaṃ puruṣaśreṣṭha dharmeṇa pratipedivān idaṃ varṣasahasrāya rājyaṃ kurukulāgatam bāla evābhijāto 'si sarvabhūtānupālakaḥ
english: "Then you, O best of men, rightfully obtained this kingdom that has come down through the Kuru lineage — you were born noble, a protector of all beings, even as a child."

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca nāsmin kule jātu babhūva rājā; yo na prajānāṃ hitakṛt priyaś ca viśeṣataḥ prekṣya pitāmahānāṃ; vṛttaṃ mahad vṛttaparāyaṇānām
english: Janamejaya said: In this family there never was a king who was not a benefactor and beloved of his subjects — as one sees by looking at the great conduct of our forefathers who were utterly devoted to right conduct.

sanskrit: kathaṃ nidhanam āpannaḥ pitā mama tathāvidhaḥ ācakṣadhvaṃ yathāvan me śrotum icchāmi tattvataḥ
english: "How did such a father of mine meet his death? Tell me truly; I wish to hear it in full."

sanskrit: sūta uvāca evaṃ saṃcoditā rājñā mantriṇas te narādhipam ūcuḥ sarve yathāvṛttaṃ rājñaḥ priyahite ratāḥ
english: The Sūta said: Thus urged by the king, all those ministers, devoted to the welfare of their lord, spoke the full account to the king.

sanskrit: babhūva mṛgayāśīlas tava rājan pitā sadā yathā pāṇḍur mahābhāgo dhanurdharavaro yudhi asmāsv āsajya sarvāṇi rājakāryāṇy aśeṣataḥ
english: "Your father, O king, was always fond of the hunt, like the greatly blessed Pāndu — the foremost of bow-bearers in battle — entrusting all royal affairs entirely to us."

sanskrit: sa kadā cid vanacaro mṛgaṃ vivyādha patriṇā viddhvā cānvasarat tūrṇaṃ taṃ mṛgaṃ gahane vane
english: "Once, while roaming the forest, he pierced a deer with an arrow, and after wounding it, he swiftly pursued that deer into the dense jungle."

sanskrit: padātir baddhanistriṃśas tatāyudhakalāpavān na cāsasāda gahane mṛgaṃ naṣṭaṃ pitā tava
english: "Going on foot, sword belted at his side, quiver of arrows strapped on, your father could not find the deer that had vanished in the thicket."

sanskrit: pariśrānto vayaḥsthaś ca ṣaṣṭivarṣo jarānvitaḥ kṣudhitaḥ sa mahāraṇye dadarśa munim antike
english: "Exhausted, advanced in years, sixty years old and feeling the weight of age, and hungry, he spotted a sage close by in the great forest."
